title: Explainable AI-based disease diagnostics using real-time plasmonic biosensor data and blockchain technology
desc: This paper proposes a secure and decentralized framework for biomedical diagnostics using plasmonic biosensor data by integrating federated learning, blockchain, post-quantum cryptography, meta-learning, and explainable AI (XAI). The proposed system addresses key limitations of centralized healthcare models, including data privacy risks, vulnerability to cyberattacks, and lack of transparency. A federated meta-learning approach is employed to improve model adaptability and accuracy across heterogeneous institutional datasets, while blockchain ensures secure data sharing, auditability, and resistance to model poisoning attacks. Additionally, a post-quantum cryptographic layer is incorporated to enhance long-term data security against emerging quantum threats. Experimental results demonstrate improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced security, and scalable performance with acceptable latency overhead. The findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enabling secure, collaborative, and trustworthy AI-driven healthcare systems.

title: Advanced optimization of drug solubility through statistical analysis using machine learning
desc: Predictive modeling of scientific systems is often difficult due to limited data, impaired bias due to shifts in the data, and commonly applied techniques used to model data for generalized solutions. A proof of concept for the aforementioned problem is provided by utilizing a new approach to data analysis and modeling development that results in more accurate solubility predictions from a physics-constrained, hybrid machine learning (ML) and statistical modeling method with added value of embedded constraints into a well-defined, flexible model. A quantitative evaluation of the methodology discussed will be conducted via interpolation, extrapolation, and noise scenarios using realistic datasets to evaluate the performance of the framework. Traditional modeling methods have provided accurate predictions but exhibited unstable and non-physical behaviors during the extrapolation and interpolation process. In contrast, the proposed approach is able to predict solubility accurately, maintain a physical relationship between pressure and solubility, and produce more accurate and robust predictions while prioritizing predictive utility instead of statistical accuracy. A predefined λ weighting factor will adjust the extent to which the methodology incorporates data-driven methodology versus physics-based guided solutions into the models.
